candidates.title: POST /presets spends a Perspective call before reserving quota; a same-dye concurrent burst is charged one submission
candidates.claim: POST /presets only runs a read-only daily-cap pre-check (presets.ts:998), then calls moderateContent/Perspective (:1031). A dye_signature UNIQUE collision then returns through respondToDuplicate (:1058-1064, :171-205) without writing a submission_events row, so N concurrent POSTs with one fresh dye set make N Perspective calls but are charged one submission. Repeating this with a new dye set for each of the 10 daily submissions lets one account drive Perspective (~1 QPS quota) to 429, which pushes other users' concurrent submissions and edits into perspective_unavailable -> pending. Palette provider answers must echo the request and be a strict #RRGGBB (appearance.js:132-150). Core's provider validates every request before any lookup (chara-palette-provider.ts:95-121).

The oauth reviewer read a4e6693 without fetching, so fetch the clone first; the memory note security-audit-check-xivauth says the clone lives in other-sources/XIVAuth, or use C:/dev/XIVProjects/XIVAuth. Also read api/v1/users_controller.rb (social_identities serialization). Questions: can a Discord identity be attached to an XIVAuth account without proving control of that Discord account? Look at the email-based auto-merge at :109-116, at whether the Discord OmniAuth strategy keeps unverified emails, and at whether one Discord external_id can be linked to two XIVAuth users. (2) oauth: apps/oauth/src/handlers/xivauth.ts:330-400 (social_identities -> linkedDiscordId), services/user-service.ts:160-289 (attach/merge rules, 'never claims an owned Discord id') and services/jwt-service.ts (which value goes in the discord_id claim when the link is refused). (3) presets-api: middleware/auth.ts:71-115,353-377 (acting id = discord_id claim, else sub), handlers/presets.ts:360-390 together with services/identity-rekey-service.ts:21-71 (rekey jwtSub -> jwtDiscordId), and middleware/ban-check.ts:48-101. candidates.title: Upstream XIVAuth email auto-merge links a new provider identity to an existing account and signs in with no owner confirmation or MFA; via oauth this yields a presets-api JWT carrying the victim's discord_id
candidates.deploy_unit: gap (upstream XIVAuth a4e6693; impact lands in oauth + presets-api)
candidates.claim: When no (provider, uid) identity exists, XIVAuth looks up any user by the provider-reported email, attaches the incoming identity to that user and signs in via sso_signin (:60-62). The MFA step exists only in sessions_controller.rb:136-150, so this skips it. Anyone holding a provider account whose 'verified' email equals a victim's XIVAuth email gets the victim's XIVAuth session. oauth then resolves the victim's row by xivauth_id (user-service.ts:73-77) and mints the victim's discord_id (jwt-service.ts:141). In presets-api that allows edit and delete (presets.ts:437,587), voting, and moderator rights if the victim is a moderator (auth.ts:365). Precondition: the attacker must control a mailbox at a provider that verifies email, or a provider that returns unverified emails. Discord gates on verified (lib/omniauth/discord.rb:23). The GitHub and Twitch gems are not vendored, so their gating is unconfirmed. This is upstream's to fix and should be reported separately; on our side it could only be narrowed.
candidates.evidence:
omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:109-116:
  email = auth.dig(:info, :email)
  return nil if email.blank?
  existing_user = User.find_for_database_authentication(email: email.downcase)
  existing_user&.add_social_identity(auth)
  existing_user
and :60-62 `sign_in_and_redirect @user` with no MFA prompt. Upstream tip confirmed with `git ls-remote origin HEAD` = a4e669343add.

candidates.title: oauth never clears or re-checks a row's Discord link, so a Discord id once attached stays the presets-api identity after XIVAuth stops asserting it
candidates.claim: attachIdentities only fills an empty discord_id and keeps existing.discord_id in every other case. A null linkedDiscordId from xivauth.ts:346 is ignored, and no route unlinks or deletes an account. Once an XIVAuth account's row holds snowflake D, that account keeps minting discord_id=D even after D is unlinked upstream (social_identities_controller.rb:4-10). D's real owner who signs in with Discord lands on the same row (findOrCreateUser step 2, user-service.ts:81-86) and cannot evict the stale xivauth_id. That only changes when a different XIVAuth account asserting D signs in (:202-208). This turns a one-time upstream mis-link (candidate 01) into permanent impersonation. With a legitimate link there is no effect.

positives: XIVAuth Discord uid always comes from Discord users/@me with the user's token (lib/omniauth/discord.rb:17,34-36); the email is kept only when Discord reports verified (:23)

XIVAuth allows one Discord uid on one user at a time: unique index (db/schema.rb:362), model validation (social_identity.rb:3) and bind refusal (omniauth_callbacks_controller.rb:72-82); OmniAuth CSRF protection is on and only steam is exempt (:2, Gemfile:84)

oauth accepts only a snowflake-shaped linked id (xivauth.ts:348); it never claims a Discord id another row owns and never overwrites one (user-service.ts:182-200); the race fallback keeps the old id (:230-247)
The JWT discord_id is the D1 row value re-read after UPDATE (user-service.ts:291, jwt-service.ts:141), so it cannot differ from what user-service accepted; a refused link mints the row's prior value
presets-api pins iss in production (wrangler.toml:76) and checks the jti blacklist (auth.ts:106-109); a sub UUID can never collide with a snowflake or a MODERATOR_IDS entry

The re-key uses sub and discord_id from one token, runs only for web auth with differing ids, has a ban pre-check plus a NOT_BANNED guard on every statement, runs as one batch, and treats a self-move as a no-op (presets.ts:371-384; identity-rekey-service.ts:22-25,45,48-69)
